{{Quote|Harnkk whoom?''"<br />"''On ''my'' authority, that's whose.|Hahrynyar, questioning Teela Kaarz's authority to alter plans to place a heat exhaust port in the polar trench of Sector N-One of the Death Star|<ref name="DS" />}}
'''Hahrynyar''' was a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] who was [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the construction of the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], where he served as the shift [[Chief/Legends|chief]] on a subsector of [[Sector N-One/Legends|Sector N-One]] on the [[Armor/Legends|armored]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], during the construction, Hahrynyar ordered an extra [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|exhaust port]] installed, which led him into a confrontation with [[Teela Kaarz]], a [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Architect/Legends|architect]], over the placement of the port. Although the Wookiee took ill with a suspected [[Parasite/Legends|parasitic]] infection before any change to the station's blueprints could be made, the exhaust port was ordered and installed as he had planned, a development that presented the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] with the means to destroy the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Arrk-arn ksh sawrron.|Hahrynyar demands to see Teela Kaarz's authority in writing|<ref name="DS" />}}
[[File:Thermal_exhaust_port.png|thumb|right|300px|The thermal exhaust port Hahrynyar was instructed to remove but never got the chance to.]]
Hahrynyar was an [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] construction worker whom the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] assigned to the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]], a massive [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] that was to be used against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He served as a shift [[Chief/Legends|chief]] on a subsector of [[Sector N-One/Legends|Sector N-One]].<ref name="DS" /> In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="Date">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']] establishes that [[Teela Kaarz]]'s request for Hahrynyar takes place less than a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].</ref> during the station's construction, Hahrynyar installed a secondary [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] below the main port, and afterward was involved in an argument with [[Teela Kaarz]], a [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Architect/Legends|architect]] who specialized in [[encapsulated arcology]], concerning the port's placement. Kaarz told the Wookiee that she had the authority to change the blueprints; Hahrynyar demanded to see that authority in [[Writing/Legends|writing]]. After the confrontation, Hahrynyar returned to his duties and ordered a crew to unpack and install equipment.<ref name="DS" />

At a later point during the construction, Hahrynyar was involved in a decompression accident that required a [[Heart/Legends|heart]]-[[Lung/Legends|lung]] transplant, which was performed by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Kornell Divini]]. The Wookiee was placed on immuno-suppressive drugs, which caused him to develop a suspected [[Parasite/Legends|parasitic]] infection. Plagued with a cough and a high fever, Hahrynyar was unable to return to work. Hahrynyar and Divini had a conversation about the former's condition, which was translated by the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[C-4ME-O]]. Divini decided to place Hahrynyar on a medicine to treat the new infection, warning Hahrynyar about several potential side effects. Hahrynyar expressed concerns over his absence to the doctor, but Divini insisted he did not return to work until they were sure he was recovered and not contagious, as Imperial protocol directed. As such, the work on the exhaust ports continued, as Kaarz had never obtained the authorization to remove them.<ref name="DS" />

Kaarz later noticed that the port had still been built and expressed frustration to the remaining crew that Hahrynyar was out of commission and had never passed on her directive. During the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the port became the target of the Rebel Alliance, as they led directly into the main [[Hypermatter/Legends|hypermatter]] [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]]. The Alliance used this weakness to their advantage during the Battle of Yavin and fired [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedos]] into the port, which triggered a chain reaction, and destroyed the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="DS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Well, the side effects are generally mild. There are a couple that might cause some discomfort.''"<br />"''Arm whoon urr.|Kornell Divini and Hahrynyar on an anti-parasitic medicine, the latter replying an idiosyncratic affirmation expressed in weary cynicism|<ref name="DS" />}}
Hahrynyar was an elderly Wookiee whose pelt had turned almost entirely [[Color/Legends|gray]] with age. He was a natural-born leader,<ref name="CSWE" /> and due to the Wookiee's attitude, Teela Kaarz suspected that Hahrynyar would have volunteered to join the Death Star construction crew even if he had not been enslaved. Grizzled and stubborn, Hahrynyar intentionally forgot how to understand [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] so that he was able to avoid communicating with his superiors. He had a dismissive and cynical sense of humor when speaking with Doctor Divini and once made a remark concerning [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] personal hygiene.<ref name="DS" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|Arrrrnn rowwlnnn.|Hahrynyar claims that a smart builder would not sweat the small stuff|<ref name="DS" />}}
Hahrynyar was a capable construction worker and Teela Kaarz believed his work had a good reputation.<ref name="DS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hahrynyar first appeared in the [[2007]] novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']], which was written by [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Steve Perry]].<ref name="DS" />
